note: Relapsed/refractory FL treated with autologous CD19 CAR-T (axi-cel, tisa-cel, liso-cel): the class was built on ALL/Burkitt xenografts and one syngeneic mouse lymphoma, never an FL model, yet the first CD19 CAR-T patient ever treated (2010) had FL.
label: Follicular lymphoma (CD19 CAR-T)

engagement.model: Syngeneic murine CD19-CAR, CD19+ B-cell lymphoma in C3H mice
engagement.note: Anti-murine-CD19 CAR T cells wiped out normal B cells in mice for 143+ days: B-cell aplasia is the engagement read-out.
engagement.short: Mouse CAR wipes out B cells
engagement.quote: One infusion of anti-CD19-CAR-transduced T cells completely eliminated normal B cells from mice for at least 143 days.
engagement.judgement: Model named in the Yescarta Summary Basis for Regulatory Action (2017, https://www.fda.gov/files/vaccines%2C%20blood%20%26%20biologics/published/October-18--2017-Summary-Basis-for-Regulatory-Action---YESCARTA.pdf), which cites this paper. The CAR in the mice is an anti-murine-CD19 construct, not the clinical FMC63 product, so product_in_model is false. NSG xenografts (Milone 2009) have no normal B cells and cannot show this read-out, so the syngeneic model is the best engagement model.

engagement.model: Syngeneic murine CD19-CAR, CD19+ B-cell lymphoma in C3H mice
engagement.note: First patient treated had follicular lymphoma: blood B cells absent 39+ weeks and immunoglobulins fell, as the mouse model said.
engagement.short: FL patient: B cells gone 39 weeks
engagement.quote: Blood B cells were absent for at least 39 weeks after anti-CD19-CAR-transduced T-cell infusion despite prompt recovery of other blood cell counts.
engagement.reason: B-cell aplasia held in FL patient
engagement.judgement: n=1 case report (NCT00924326, results first posted 2019-03-21); the case report never mentions the mouse model (full text read), so comparison_stated is false and this is my juxtaposition. The same group's 2012 series (https://doi.org/10.1182/blood-2011-10-384388; 4 of 8 patients FL, 4 of 8 with long-term B-cell depletion) states the comparison itself: 'Similar to the murine studies, these early clinical reports have suggested an anti-malignancy effect'. A stricter re-score that requires a stated comparison moves this entry to 2012, not to untested. Medium confidence because n=1 and direction only.

dose.model: NALM-6 ALL xenograft in NSG mice
dose.note: Cell doses were titrated in NALM-6 mice, but clinical doses came from escalation; no exposure or occupancy target was ever carried to patients.
dose.short: Cell dose set in clinic, not mice
dose.quote: In an immunodeficient mouse xenograft model of primary human pre-B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, human T cells expressing anti-CD19 CARs containing CD137 exhibited the greatest antileukemic efficacy and prolonged (>6 months) survival in vivo
dose.judgement: Milone 2009 is the CD19-4-1BB-zeta construct that became tisagenlecleucel, so product_in_model is true. The Kymriah SBRA (2017, https://www.fda.gov/media/107962/download) lists 'assessment of in vivo anti-tumor activity of KYMRIAH in mouse xenograft tumor models' and persistence in tumor-bearing mice, but neither the Kymriah nor the Yescarta review derives a human cell dose from animals; no published comparison of a model exposure target with patient exposure exists for FL (abstract-level reading of the FL trials: ELARA and TRANSCEND FL report cellular kinetics without any animal reference).

efficacy.model: NALM-6 ALL xenograft in NSG mice
efficacy.note: The class's pivotal preclinical efficacy was in NALM-6 ALL (tisa-cel) and Raji/NALM-6 (liso-cel) xenografts; no follicular-lymphoma model was ever used.
efficacy.short: ALL/Burkitt xenografts, never an FL model
efficacy.quote: In an immunodeficient mouse xenograft model of primary human pre-B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, human T cells expressing anti-CD19 CARs containing CD137 exhibited the greatest antileukemic efficacy and prolonged (>6 months) survival in vivo
efficacy.judgement: Liso-cel's preclinical paper (Sommermeyer 2016, https://doi.org/10.1038/leu.2015.247) also used NSG xenografts of ALL/Burkitt lines. A PubMed search for CD19 CAR-T in an FL xenograft or PDX returned only Araujo-Ayala 2026 (https://doi.org/10.1182/blood.2025032663, academic ARI-0001 dual CD19-CD70 CAR), published after all three products were approved: no FL-specific model was used by any of the three programs.

efficacy.model: Syngeneic murine CD19-CAR, CD19+ B-cell lymphoma in C3H mice
efficacy.note: FL patient's lymphoma regressed (partial remission, 32 weeks) as the syngeneic mouse lymphoma had; direction matched, cure did not.
efficacy.short: FL lymphoma regressed as mouse did
efficacy.quote: After therapy, computed tomography scans revealed an impressive partial remission of the lymphoma that lasted 32 weeks
efficacy.judgement: Mice were cured (large subcutaneous masses eradicated); the patient had a 32-week PR then CD19+ progression, so magnitude is direction_only. The case report does not cite the mouse work (comparison_stated false); Kochenderfer 2012 (https://doi.org/10.1182/blood-2011-10-384388, 4 FL patients, 6 of 8 remissions) states it: 'Similar to the murine studies, these early clinical reports have suggested an anti-malignancy effect'. Later FL trials agree in direction but none compares with a model: ZUMA-5 ORR 92%/CR 74% (Jacobson 2022, https://doi.org/10.1016/S1470-2045(21)00591-X; NCT03105336 results first posted 2025-12-23), ELARA CRR 69.1% (Fowler 2022, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-021-01622-0; NCT03568461 results first posted 2022-07-22), TRANSCEND FL ORR 97% (Morschhauser 2024, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-024-02986-9; NCT04245839, no results posted as of 2026-11-02). Status stays 'same', not 'neg': no CD19 CAR-T has failed in FL for the model to have flagged.

safety.model: Syngeneic murine CD19-CAR, CD19+ B-cell lymphoma in C3H mice
safety.note: The filed model predicted only B-cell aplasia; FDA review: mice showed no overt toxicity. Xenografts cannot show CRS (no human myeloid cells).
safety.short: Mice: B-cell aplasia, no other toxicity
safety.quote: One infusion of anti-CD19-CAR-transduced T cells completely eliminated normal B cells from mice for at least 143 days.
safety.judgement: Yescarta clinical review (2017, https://www.fda.gov/media/109149/download), section 4.3: 'The mice did not show any overt signs of toxicity.' Kymriah SBRA (2017, https://www.fda.gov/media/107962/download): 'No safety concerns were identified in the resulting data from the nonclinical studies.' Both products were filed on models silent beyond B-cell aplasia.

safety.model: Syngeneic murine CD19-CAR, CD19+ B-cell lymphoma in C3H mice
safety.note: FL patient: B-cell aplasia and hypogammaglobulinemia as predicted; otherwise only a 2-day fever and chemotherapy cytopenias, matching the quiet mice.
safety.quote: Consistent with eradication of B-lineage cells, serum immunoglobulins decreased to very low levels after treatment.
safety.judgement: Full text (PMC2993617): 'The only acute toxicities that the patient experienced were cytopenias that were attributable to chemotherapy' plus a 2-day fever to 38.5 C. For this one patient the model's prediction (B-cell aplasia) and its silence (nothing else) both held; n=1, juxtaposed by me.

safety.model: Syngeneic murine CD19-CAR, CD19+ B-cell lymphoma in C3H mice
safety.note: Same NCI trial, 4 of 8 patients FL: hypotension, obtundation, renal failure, capillary leak with IFN-gamma/TNF surges the model never showed.
safety.short: Cytokine toxicity the mice never showed
safety.quote: Anti-CD19-CAR-transduced T cells have great promise to improve the treatment of B-cell malignancies because of a potent ability to eradicate CD19(+) cells in vivo; however, reversible cytokine-associated toxicities occurred after CAR-transduced T-cell infusions.
safety.judgement: Full text (PMC3327450) Table 1: patients 1, 2 and 8 had FL (patient 1 treated twice); Table 4: FL patient 8 had 'Hypotension, obtundation, acute renal failure, capillary leak syndrome' with prominent IFN-gamma/TNF elevations, i.e. CRS plus neurotoxicity in an FL patient. The paper juxtaposes the mouse efficacy data but never says the model missed the toxicity, so comparison_stated is false; the silence is documented by the FDA (Yescarta review: 'The mice did not show any overt signs of toxicity.'). Epub 2011-12-08, print 2012 (Blood 119:2709). Later FL trials confirm the miss without any model comparison: ZUMA-5 grade>=3 CRS 7%, grade 3-4 neurologic events 19% (Jacobson 2022; NCT03105336 results first posted 2025-12-23); ELARA CRS 48.5% (grade>=3 0%), ICANS 4.1% (Fowler 2022; NCT03568461 results first posted 2022-07-22); TRANSCEND FL CRS 58% (grade>=3 1%), neurologic events 15% (Morschhauser 2024; NCT04245839 no results posted). The CRS/neurotoxicity mouse models (Giavridis 2018 SCID-beige/Raji, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-018-0041-7; Norelli 2018 humanized NSG/ALL, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-018-0036-4, 'hampered by the lack of appropriate animal models') were built after the fact in ALL/Burkitt settings and have never been compared with FL patients; FL's milder CRS than DLBCL/ALL was not predicted by any model. Contra overrides the 2010 match per the rules.
